item.text:
**Assessment**
Mixed, leaning positive. In 2024 Jokowi’s administration had credible evidence of improved access in health, social protection targeting, education re-entry, and some WASH/nutrition gains. But access remained uneven, especially for safe water/sanitation, remote areas, and Papua, and housing evidence is mostly planning-stage rather than realized access.

**Claims**
- [Indonesia](https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2024-2025/country-profile/2024/indonesia) - World Health Organization, 2024. WHO says Indonesia reached 90% coverage, lowered out-of-pocket costs, and improved access to quality essential health services regardless of gender, age, or disability. IDs: `6B.2`
- [Does Indonesia’s National Health Insurance Scheme mobile phone application, Mobile JKN, support health financing?](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240100893) - World Health Organization, 2024-12-06. JKN was designed to expand health access and financial protection; Mobile JKN made registration and informal-sector payments easier and reduced administrative costs, supporting broader access to care. IDs: `6B.2`
- [BAPPENAS Perkuat Dukungan untuk Anak-Anak dan Keluarga Rentan](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/id/press-releases/bappenas-perkuat-dukungan-untuk-anak-anak-dan-keluarga-rentan) - UNICEF Indonesia, 2024-04-25. Regsosek was presented as a way to improve targeting and delivery of social assistance for poor and vulnerable households, including those affected by shocks. IDs: `6B.2`
- [A Blueprint to Get Children Back to School in Indonesia](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/stories/blueprint-get-children-back-school-indonesia) - UNICEF Indonesia, 2024-08-23. The government-led back-to-school movement helped return nearly 37,000 children to learning and prevented about 149,000 from dropping out since 2021, though 3.9 million out-of-school children still signals a large gap. IDs: `6B.2`
- [WASH Acts – Edisi 2024](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/id/wash/laporan/wash-acts-edisi-2024) - UNICEF Indonesia, 2025-04. Open defecation fell from 4.2% to 3.2% in 2024, but safely managed water and sanitation remained very low, indicating partial progress rather than broad basic-service access. IDs: `6B.2`
- [Nutrition](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/nutrition) - UNICEF Indonesia, accessed 2026. The page says Indonesia has made significant nutrition progress over the past decade, but the country still faces the triple burden of malnutrition and more than 4.5 million stunted children, so food-security/nutrition gains are incomplete. IDs: `6B.2`
- [How the Gap Fund supported the design of green, resilient, and affordable homes in Indonesia](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/12/03/green-homes-resilient-cities-tackling-indonesia-housing-crisis) - World Bank, 2024-12-03. The Bank describes Indonesia as facing a housing crisis but says new tools and guidelines were developed for affordable, energy-efficient homes and could support a 1 million green homes program by 2030. IDs: `6B.2`
- [Social Protection Inclusion in Indonesia’s Remote Areas - Identifying and Addressing Gaps and Challenges](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099062624071020814) - World Bank, 2024-06-01. The report says poor and vulnerable households in remote areas still face barriers to accessing social protection, so access improved in design terms but remained uneven in practice. IDs: `6B.2`
- [Indonesia health accounts 2024: Strengthening evidence for sustainable health financing](https://www.who.int/indonesia/news-room/item/12-02-2026-indonesia-health-accounts-2024--strengthening-evidence-for-sustainable-health-financing) - World Health Organization, 2026-02-12. The 2024 health accounts show public financing remained the backbone of health care and out-of-pocket spending declined, which supports a view of better health access and financial protection in 2024. IDs: `6B.2`

**Negative / limiting evidence**
- [Indonesia: Racism, Discrimination Against Indigenous Papuans](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/18/indonesia-racism-discrimination-against-indigenous-papuans) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-09-18. HRW says security-force abuse, displacement, and weak accountability in Papua continued, which undercuts any claim of broadly improved welfare access for all groups. IDs: `6B.2`
- [Indonesia’s Learning Poverty Brief 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099082924151529593) - World Bank/UNESCO, 2024-04-01. The brief frames learning poverty as a continuing threat to human capital and poverty reduction, showing that education access and learning quality still needed major repair. IDs: `6B.2`
- [Indonesia’s out-of-school children story](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/stories/blueprint-get-children-back-school-indonesia) - UNICEF Indonesia, 2024-08-23. The same education program underscores the scale of the problem: 3.9 million out-of-school children remained a major access gap even amid progress. IDs: `6B.2`

**Search gap**
Direct 2024 evidence is strongest for health, education re-entry, WASH, and social-protection targeting. It is weaker for housing and food security as realized household access outcomes; those domains are mostly supported by planning, nutrition, or program-design evidence rather than clean nationwide access metrics.
